sentences.text: The tip of the upper jaw was slender and needle-like, formed by the premaxilla bones, which are the front bones of the snout.
Each upper jaw had only eight teeth and a straight lower margin, unlike the strongly curved margins seen in other pterosaurs.
The skull featured a sagittal crest with grooves and a concave leading margin, a ridge running along the top of the skull.
The holotype specimen, found near Urumqi in the southern Junggar Basin, consists of the front of a skull and lower jaws from a large individual with an estimated total skull length of 400 mm.
The genus name means "lance-jaw lizard" in Greek, while the specific name acutirostris means "needle snout" in Latin, both referring to the animal's pointed jaws.
The genus Lonchognathosaurus was named in 2004 by Michael Maisch, Andreas Matzke, and Sun Ge, with the type species being Lonchognathosaurus acutirostris.
In 2021, Augustin et al. described postcranial elements from the Lianmuqin Formation that confirmed the validity of the genus and provided new anatomical information.
Cladistic analysis classifies Lonchognathosaurus as a member of the family Dsungaripteridae and the sister taxon to Dsungaripterus.
Lonchognathosaurus lived during the Aptian to Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous in the Lianmuqin Formation of Xinjiang, China.
The time range for Lonchognathosaurus is estimated from 137.05 to 100.5 million years ago, spanning the Valanginian to Albian stages.
Averianov et al. (2022) identified a wing metacarpal fragment from the Ilek Formation in West Siberia as possibly belonging to Lonchognathosaurus due to its near identity with the type species.
Brian Andres argues that Lonchognathosaurus is a junior synonym of Dsungaripterus weii.
